source: creator-approved chat copy plus orchestrated parallel visual room on 2026-07-20

concept.title: Not Married Yet, Already Us
concept.human_truth: Long before vows, two people begin behaving like a unit through automatic habits, shared stress, real friction, and care that survives irritation.
concept.emotional_arc: unofficial habits -> mutual decisions -> one problem becomes shared stress -> friction -> care persists -> already an us
concept.visual_system: Wordless Habit Relay with a broken-key continuity sequence and a circular doorway payoff

visual_setup: Premium observational-intimacy watercolor-and-ink on neutral warm ivory paper. Rich staged behavior, not quote-card posing. Non-repeating shot ladder. Slides 4-10 are one continuous broken-key incident with one wardrobe; slides 1-3 and 11 are separate moments with different wardrobe. Every native 1080x1440 and separate 1080x1920 image must contain exact integrated text plus tiny top-right @a.storyof.two.

slides.copy:
We’re not married yet.
But try telling that to our habits.
slides.visual: Wide three-quarter apartment doorway scene: Aachu slips Zuv's wallet and keys into his waiting jacket pocket while Zuv simultaneously lowers her filled water bottle into her open tote. Neither looks at the other; their crossed forearms and automatic timing prove muscle memory. Couple in lower half, clean ivory negative space above-left, brandmark clear top-right.
slides.continuity_lock: Separate montage moment; use casual going-out clothes sourced from selected identity references. Preserve only a two-inch height difference.

slides.copy:
Every plan starts with:
“Ek minute, usse poochna padega.”
slides.visual: Over-shoulder threshold view from outside: Aachu is halfway through the exit, one palm raised to the unseen outside world in a natural one-second gesture, while turning back toward Zuv. Zuv stands several feet inside holding two helmets and gives a familiar nod. The check-in reads as alignment, never permission.
slides.continuity_lock: New montage scene and outfit; no app UI, speech bubble, driver, or extra text.

slides.copy:
Every small decision becomes
a two-person meeting.
slides.visual: Wide profile hallway scene: Zuv holds a small blank framed print against the wall while Aachu stands several feet back, squinting with mock seriousness and pinching two fingers to signal two centimetres left. Their eye-lines converge on the frame; subtle painter's-tape alternatives show mutual over-investment without clutter.
slides.continuity_lock: New montage scene and outfit; frame contains no writing.

slides.visual: Tight over-Zuv-shoulder landing shot at lock level: he remains upright, frozen at the apartment lock, holding half of a snapped key while the other half is unmistakably stuck. Aachu is not yet visible. The solitary reaction establishes one person's problem before it spreads.
slides.continuity_lock: Start of one continuous incident through slide 10; lock the same clothes and apartment landing architecture.

slides.visual: High three-quarter landing view: the broken key remains in the lock. Both stay upright. Aachu searches her tote for a spare or maintenance number while Zuv lights the lock with his phone torch and examines it without forcing it. Their shoulders nearly touch and both eye-lines fix on the same obstacle; neither rescues the other.
slides.continuity_lock: Same incident, door, snapped key, and clothes as slide 4; no scattered receipts or crouched pose.

slides.visual: Low-medium two-shot along the same landing: Aachu holds out a blank maintenance card while Zuv holds the snapped key and argues for another solution. They stand two to three feet apart with direct eye-line, equal irritation, open palms, and no finger-pointing. The failed lock sits between their competing solutions.
slides.continuity_lock: Same incident and wardrobe; no shouting, cruelty, saintly Zuv, or dramatic Aachu caricature.

slides.copy:
Then five minutes later:
“Ghar pahunch ke text karna.”
slides.visual: Wide view from inside the now-open doorway toward the stairwell: Zuv is already two steps down, body facing away with helmet in hand. Aachu remains in the doorway, posture still stiff, but instinctively calls after him. He stops mid-step and turns back immediately; their eye-lines reconnect across the distance.
slides.continuity_lock: Same incident and wardrobe; do not make it a breakup or use dialogue bubbles.

slides.copy:
Kyunki gussa apni jagah.
“Tum theek ho?” apni jagah.
slides.visual: Intimate waist-up profile at the threshold: both still look mildly annoyed and avoid a romantic gaze. Aachu notices a tiny nick on Zuv's thumb from the broken key and offers a tissue while Zuv braces the heavy door so it cannot swing into her. Their simultaneous gestures show anger and concern occupying the same frame; their hands nearly meet without an embrace.
slides.continuity_lock: Same incident and wardrobe; no smile, hug, maternal pose, instant reconciliation, or medical drama.

slides.visual: Very wide architectural landing shot: Aachu stands inside her doorway and Zuv pauses several steps away near the stairs, still connected by eye-line and each holding one of the other's everyday belongings. The physical space honestly shows two separate lives; the exchanged objects show the unofficial unit already operating.
slides.continuity_lock: Same incident and wardrobe; no rings, wedding décor, embrace, split-screen divider, or posed romance.

slides.copy:
Shaadi abhi baaki hai.
Par “hum” toh kab ke ban chuke hain.
slides.visual: Circular visual echo of slide 1 on another morning and in different clothes: at the same doorway, Aachu passes Zuv his wallet while Zuv passes her water bottle in the same automatic crossed-hand relay. This time a repaired key hangs quietly beside the door and both share the smallest knowing smile. The visual closes the story through repeated behavior, not a wedding symbol or generic embrace.
slides.continuity_lock: New day and outfit; deliberately echo slide 1 composition while showing the repaired-key consequence from the middle sequence.

copy.caption_recommended: No vows yet. Bas habits ne thoda jaldi decide kar liya. 🤍
copy.caption_alt: Officially, not married. Unofficially, every plan, problem, fight and check-in already comes in plural.
